reviews.title: No support, only AI
reviews.text: I tried to reach out to support with a problem and there’s just a worthless AI chatbot so I canceled my subscription entirely. Life is too short to waste it on AI.

reviews.title: Subscription ruined device
reviews.text: For something that costs what it does, having to purchase a subscription to use basic features like displaying photos feels egregious. If it wasn’t a gift, I would’ve already returned it.

reviews.title: Subscription Scam
reviews.text: Like many products and services these days corporations and they like do not want you to own anything. They want you to keep paying for their services while you actually own the actual hardware. They tie you to a subscription so that they have a never-ending source of an income. They want to drain every single dollar out of you and Skylight app. Without the subscription it’s just simply a calendar that you can’t do much with.

reviews.title: Could be better for price
reviews.text: We use skylight in our kitchen and the app. I like the photos and calendar functions.  I think the task lists could have better functionality such as priority and sorting by due date.  Everything goes in one giant list and I have to scroll to see tasks that are due first.  The grocery list function isn’t great, doesn’t  sort by area.  The recipe import doesn’t work very well, not as good as other recipe apps, no pictures and no step by step screens, just text.  No sorting functionality based on cuisine or ingredient. I do like taking pictures of calendars and it puts the data in the calendar for me with sidekick. For the price, I wish I liked it more and could replace other apps in paying for separately.

reviews.title: Horrible Customer Support
reviews.text: This company has the worst customer support I have ever encountered. It’s a combination of front-end AI and backend-end, overseas choppy email responses. I would not recommend this software or the purchase of any of their hardware.

reviews.title: Pay to play
reviews.text: One thing I love about the calendar is the photos I find it frustrating you have to pay a subscription to utilize part of the device that you purchased.

reviews.title: Beware if using for photos
reviews.text: After 1 year they want you to pay a $75 yearly subscription to display photos. I find this offensive and am frustrated with this.

reviews.title: No unpaid functionality
reviews.text: Not a single remote function for a picture frame for free. Why would I want to pay $3 a month to shut a frame off remotely.  It’s going into the trash. The quality is also poor next to aura.  You can’t control from your phone and the pictures are brassy.

reviews.title: Poorly made app
reviews.text: We switched to the Skylight app after using FamilyWall for the last 3 to 4 years because we bought a Skylight device. The calendar and menus are nowhere near as user-friendly or intuitive and the notification system is useless. furthermore, it is very frustrating than in order to ask the calendar and you must have Internet access so if you were out and about in a dead area, you cannot see your calendar.

reviews.title: To Be Desired
reviews.text: There’s some funky stuff within the application that AI could straighten out. When I add ingredients to the grocery list from creating a meal plan, I have to walk my way around the app to get back to finishing my meals list. Thats something an auto redirect or quick button on the grocery list screen could fix. Then there’s the processing time. Sure you can document a well thought out meal plan, but how long is it going to take you to do it when the lag time between clicking on the meal or recipe increases each time you add stuff to the grocery list. If you have the patience, bless you. In a world of AI and advances in processing, I am hoping these types of issues will be addressed in a not too distant future update.

reviews.title: Another way to duplicate your data
reviews.text: This apps only usable feature is that it can replicate your data from connected accounts, but you have to go through several menus to access the calendar. The calendar setup itself was not intuitive and resulted in a dozen different labels for a single account. The meal planner was the only thing I was really interested in, but without a trial to test it I’m not interested in it. I’m not going to pay a monthly subscription for another AI platform when I can ask any other free AI for a weekly meal plan.

reviews.title: Crashing app
reviews.text: At one point, the app work perfectly… But for the last month, it has been crashing every time and every time you try to send images, photos to your picture frame… please fix ASAP….. there’s a grandmother that needs to see her grandchildren!!!

reviews.title: Big List Miss
reviews.text: As I’m sure is the case for many families, the weekly grocery items and even some “to-do’s” repeat (e.g., 1/4ly tax payments). These repeating items are lost forever once completed, and so have to be retyped into the app, which is way more effort than just jotting down an item. A master list, with the ability to select only the items needed for that week or the the next grocery trip without modifying the master list, would be infinitely more helpful and would require just a few more programming steps. Please do! Also, another time saver that is found on so many other apps: a voice recording feature instead of only typing in a new item

reviews.text:
I purchased my first Skylight frame 3 years ago and since then have purchased the calendar and another frame. Now I have two purchase TWO subscriptions to get all the features on my devices. 
It really feels like Skylight is screwing their loyal customers.

reviews.title: The task list
reviews.text:
I really wanted to love the Skylight Calendar because the concept is fantastic. The calendar itself is helpful for keeping our family organized, and the task/chore feature was one of the main reasons we purchased it.

Unfortunately, the task system has been a constant source of frustration. No matter how carefully I set up recurring chores and assignments for my children, the tasks eventually become inaccurate. Chores will duplicate unexpectedly, children end up being assigned the same task multiple times, or the workload becomes uneven between family members. Instead of helping us manage responsibilities, I often find myself spending extra time troubleshooting and correcting assignments.

Another challenge is the lack of visibility into upcoming chores for each child. When trying to review responsibilities, there doesn’t appear to be a simple way to see a clear overview of all future assigned tasks for an individual child. Instead, I have to manually check day by day, which is time-consuming and makes it difficult to verify that assignments are correct.

The idea behind the feature is excellent, but the execution needs improvement. More reliable recurring task management, better prevention of duplicate assignments, and a dedicated child-specific task overview would make this feature much more useful for families.

I hope Skylight continues improving the chore system because it has the potential to be one of the strongest features of the platform.

reviews.title: Major room for improvement
reviews.text:
Skylight has a lot of potential and works well as a shared household hub, but it needs stronger communication and task-management tools to truly shine.

A sticky note or quick note feature would be incredibly helpful for fast, informal communication between shared users. This is a big one! 

Live, real-time notifications are also essential, as it’s currently too easy for tasks or updates to be missed. At the moment, notifications are limited to the calendar, with no alerts coming from Lists — even though Lists are a primary area of communication.

The Lists feature needs to be far more intuitive, including the ability to prioritize tasks (pin, reorder, or mark urgency by color or level), as well as the option to add images for visual reference.

We currently use Lists for the majority of our communication, and there feels like a major gap in what’s possible here. Most people using a system like this need multiple, flexible ways to communicate across calendars, day-to-day tasks, and items with varying levels of urgency.

A live, running daily list that shows tasks being completed in real time would greatly improve day-to-day coordination.

Additionally, completed tasks should offer more control. There should be an option to remove items permanently or archive them by day, rather than displaying every completed task from all previous days in one continuous list.

reviews.title: Get an Aura Frame Instead
reviews.text:
It’s difficult to describe how much I loathe this app. I asked for an Aura frame but was gifted a Skylight. I have gone with it because of that, but if I had bought it myself, I’d have returned it.

The biggest issue with this app is it has a very hard time receiving pictures. Every time I send pictures it “fails to true” 6-10x before all the pictures go through. From what I’ve read, this is because I am sending Live Photos. But there is absolutely no world where I have the time to export all the photos on my phone to a different format before sending them to the Skylight. This is supposed to be easy so it is frankly ridiculous the developers haven’t figured out how to fix this.

The other REALLY ANNOYING thing about this is that on your frame itself, if you randomize the photos, it shows the same 40 pictures over and over again (even though I have literally thousands on mine). So the only way to show all your photos is if you have it shows them chronologically. But if you’ve gotten the “failed to true” error, your photos won’t be in order. And if you send any older photos, they will also be out of order. The frame and the gallery in the app can’t actually organize by when the photo was truly taken.

Also 90% of the features of the app are behind a subscription based paywall. This whole frame is such an absolute scam, it makes my blood boil. Pick literally any other brand.

reviews.title: Disappointed After a Year of Use – Leaving Despite the Investment
reviews.text:
After using Skylight for just over a year, I'm sadly moving on despite the significant financial investment. I utilized all the calendar features—meal planning, tasks, and events—but persistent issues have made it unsustainable.
The core problem is twofold: the features are inherently buggy, and updates appear to lack proper quality assurance. Too often, new updates break existing functionality, forcing users to rebuild their entire system from scratch.
The most recent example: tasks were previously ordered by creation time, allowing me to arrange both routines and chores in my preferred sequence. When the new drag-and-drop feature was released (only for routines), this ordering disappeared entirely, with no alternative way to organize chores. This marks the third time I've faced starting over completely—a process that takes 4+ hours each time. At this point, the app creates more work than it saves.
Customer support has been unhelpful. While I understand Skylight is a small team, that doesn't excuse releasing half-baked features that disrupt the user experience. Quality should come before new functionality, especially for a productivity tool people rely on daily.
I genuinely wanted this to work, but I can't continue investing time into an app that repeatedly undermines its own purpose.

reviews.title: Oh-So-Buggy 🐞

Lists keep crashing. Sometimes don’t show up at all. Often can’t drag to rearrange a list. Rendering it pretty much useless. 

Also kind of wish I could sort between oldest or alphabetical order.

reviews.title: Edit feature in app does not work and the frame changes photo colors!
reviews.text: I have had this frame since April and these issues have been ongoing and they are VERY basic requirements. First, you CANNOT edit photos in the app. Not even a simple crop, it makes them incredibly grainy and pixelated. Second, when you upload a photo it changes the colors! Usually it changes it to a green or red tint, which is super annoying because as a photo frame it should at the very least show the true colors of the photos. It makes photos of people especially look really weird. I really really regret this purchase, as I bought two of these frames for my parents and in laws. A few other gripes- the frame is not 9:16 as they advertise but some other, random dimension, so you cannot crop your photos to fit perfectly. There should be an option to “fill” the frame. Also, most photos we take these days are with our phones and are vertical but the crop feature doesn’t even offer that as a choice. I have my frames set up vertically so the photos will fill the frames, but again; have to do all editing in my photos app before uploading. Also, once uploaded you cannot change the order of the photos as they pop up in the frame. Finally, they want to upcharge you to get other very basic features, like remote settings etc. I have reached out to customer support multiple times and they cannot seem to figure out how to fix these VERY basic issues.
